From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Private/appliance readiness: hardware refresh, offline upgrades & maintenance — post-call recap

Hi Samira — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call on private (air-gapped) deployment requirements. Please correct me if I mis-stated anything.

TL;DR: Biogenix is leaning toward a Private on-prem appliance with strict offline upgrade windows. We need to confirm hardware refresh cadence, firmware upgrade process (airgapped), and operational responsibilities for in-place upgrades vs swap-based refresh.

Key notes from the call:
- Deployment mode: Private (air-gapped) appliance pinned to Redwood Private control plane; no outbound telemetry except signed audit bundles (agreed scope).
- Hardware baseline: 2 x 4U appliances for prod (N+1), 1 x staging appliance. Customer provided preliminary inventory (please attach final).
- Firmware & BIOS updates: Customer prefers local-console upgrades during quarterly maintenance windows; wants documented MOP for each update.
- Offline upgrade path: Redwood can provide offline upgrade bundles (signed, checksummed) and a binary-based MOP; customer prefers swap-and-seed option to reduce onsite downtime where possible.
- Rollback and validation: Staged rollout in staging, smoke test acceptance criteria, and 24-hour rollback window for major version updates.
- Security/compliance: HSM/KMS integration necessary; no external key escrow. SOC2 artifacts required for procurement.

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Biogenix to share final hardware inventory spreadsheet and preferred maintenance windows — Samira / Mark (by 2026-11-12) — attached: biogenix-internal-hw-inventory.xlsx.
2) Redwood to draft MOP and offline upgrade flow (swap vs in-place) + firmware compatibility matrix — Marissa / Vivek (deliver draft by 2026-11-15).
3) Schedule 60-min technical walk-through on the MOP with Biogenix ops team — Ben to coordinate (target week of 11/16).
4) Exchange minimal SOC2 evidence and list of required controls for procurement packet — Neha to own (by 2026-11-18).

Open Qs we promised to follow up on:
- Does Biogenix require Redwood engineers onsite for swap-based refreshes or will local datacenter ops handle chassis swaps?
- Are there any regulatory constraints that would disallow signed binaries or require on-site code signing procedures?
- Preferred NTP/clock sync policies for offline fleet?

Attachments: I attached the inventory file you dropped on the call. We will also attach the initial MOP draft in the next email.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private/appliance readiness: hardware refresh, offline upgrades & maintenance — post-call recap

Ben — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications and answers below.

Clarifications / answers:
- Onsite swaps: Our datacenter ops team will perform chassis swaps and power cycles; we do not want external engineers on-site for routine refreshes. For any firmware that requires console interaction we will assign an ops lead to work via VPN into our jump host during the scheduled window (no remote access from Redwood machines).
- Signed binaries: We are fine with Redwood-provided signed upgrade bundles as long as we can validate signatures locally and the process is fully documented (checksums + signing cert fingerprint).
- NTP: We operate isolated NTP stratum servers; Redwood should sign bundles in a way that does not require contacting external time services.
- Compliance docs: I attached a redacted inventory and a short list of controls we need in the procurement packet. See attachment: biogenix-internal-hw-inventory.xlsx.

Request: Can Redwood provide the MOP draft and a simple acceptance checklist we can use in staging? Also confirm whether the offline upgrade bundle will include a pre-check script and a post-check report.

Thanks,
Samira
Head of Platform Ops | Biogenix Therapeutics

Subject: Draft MOP & matrix: biogenix private deployment (internal)

Team — looping in internal notes after reviewing Samira's inventory. I started the MOP draft and attached the compatibility matrix. High-level thoughts:

1) Upgrade approach: propose swap-and-seed for major releases (>= X.Y), in-place patching for minor fixes. Swap reduces risk and minimizes service interruption but requires disk re-seeding and validation.
2) Pre-checks (to include in bundle): hardware model check, firmware version snapshot, RAID/SMART health, hash of current image, staging smoke tests.
3) Post-checks: tokenization smoke test, KV cache warmup verification, endpoint latency baseline.
4) Rollback: maintain previous image on standby appliance for 48 hours post-upgrade; automated rollback script if health-check fails.
5) Firmware/BIOS: Vivek — need to confirm whether Redwood will ship vendor-specific firmware blobs or provide guidance only. If Redwood ships blobs we must include vendor EULA and versioning metadata in the bundle.

I've attached: MOP_draft_biogenix_v1.docx and firmware-compatibility-matrix.csv. Please review and add comments by COB Monday (2026-11-15). I'll schedule the walkthrough for mid-next-week once we have a consolidated draft.

Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: Draft MOP & matrix: biogenix private deployment (internal)

Quick notes from infra/engineering POV:
- We can produce signed offline bundles containing the Redwood runtime + model artifacts and a separate vendor firmware zip. For vendor firmware we need confirmation that Biogenix accepts a vendor-supplied blob (we do not re-sign vendor firmware).
- BIOS updates that require interactive console steps: we should document exact keystrokes and have Biogenix ops assigned for the window. We will provide a remote-run checklist (no remote access).
- Image seeding: propose we include a checksum-verified seed image and an rsync-friendly delta for subsequent minor updates to keep transfer sizes small.
- Smoke tests: we'll include a pre-check script and post-check report generator as Samira requested. The post-check will emit a signed archive that Biogenix can forward to their audit team.

Action items: Vivek to add firmware signing/packaging section to MOP (ETA 2026-11-15). Ben to lock meeting time with Biogenix for 11/17 or 11/18. Neha to prep SOC2 delta for procurement.

-Vivek
